title: History of the World in the 20th Century

sections.headline: War in Europe! America Vows Neutrality
paragraphs: Western Europe fell to the German Blitzkrieg, which then turned to invade the Soviet Union. President Roosevelt vowed to keep America out of the war and lifted the Japanese oil embargo even as their forces expanded into mainland China. With Roosevelt’s focus on peace and neutrality, the secret “Manhattan Project” was quietly disbanded.

sections.headline: Hitler Assassinated! Germany Retains Control
paragraphs: After a disastrous, failed attempt to invade Britain, the frozen, starving German army was being ground down in the ferocious Battle of Moscow. Shocking the world, Hitler was assassinated by desperate elements of the German high command. Even as de-Nazification proceeded, the celebrations were short-lived. It became clear that the new German leadership had no intention of relinquishing their battlefield gains.

sections.headline: United Europe and Pacific Reconciliation
paragraphs: After growing resistance movements across Europe, the Treaty of Berlin restored national sovereignty across Europe while retaining German influence and supremacy. This paved the way for a formal alliance and a United Europe (UE).

The European treaty formed the basis for an armistice agreement between Japan and China. Japan agreed to withdraw from its increasingly untenable occupation in exchange for trade concessions, mutual non-aggression agreements, and an uneasy peace.

sections.headline: Russia Resurgent
paragraphs: Still recovering from catastrophic losses during WWII, Stalin reorganized the remaining Soviet states into the Union of Eurasian Republics (UER). Vowing to never again be subject to a devastating invasion, the Union began an armament campaign and aggressively absorbed neighboring nations.

sections.headline: African Forces Triumphant in Suez
paragraphs: President Nasser of Egypt seized control of the Suez Canal. Both UE and UER forces contested the move, but well-organized, well-equipped forces from Nigeria and the newly formed Pan-African Federation (PAF) pushed them back. The incident accelerated anti-colonial efforts in Africa and globally, signifying the emergence of a new global power.

sections.headline: Andean-Atlantic Confederation
paragraphs: Rejecting American influence and inspired by the rising African federation, Central and South American nations formed their own military alliance. A newly elected revolutionary government in Spain shocked Europe and the world by joining the new confederation. Argentine bombers arrived in Spain to deter the gathering UE armor divisions, formalizing the new Andean-Atlantic Confederation (AAC).

sections.headline: Greater Pacific Commonwealth
paragraphs: Years of trade and mutual-defense agreements turned ancient rivalries in Asia into wary partnerships. The Australian government, increasingly isolated from Britain, proposed that the region's nations form a formal military and trade alliance: the Greater Pacific Commonwealth (GPC). Chile, increasingly at odds with AAC leadership in Brazil, opted to join its trade partners in the alliance.
India, finding itself surrounded by allied military powers, was forced to abandon neutrality and sign a mutual-defense agreement with the Pan-African Federation.

sections.headline: The Arctic War and North Atlantic Alliance
paragraphs: Using pressure campaigns, propaganda, and mass infiltration, followed by a sudden show of force, UER forces swept in and seized control of Norway, Sweden, and the Alaskan territory.

The American populace was outraged. A new administration vowed to end America’s non-intervention policies and fiercely defend American interests at home and abroad. The United States began a massive rearmament campaign and signed an agreement with Britain to form the North Atlantic Alliance (NAA).

sections.headline: Growing Tensions
paragraphs: Simmering tensions ignited in skirmishes and standoffs worldwide. The American armada bound for Alaska was turned back by a GPC blockade. United Europe forces amassed to challenge AAC and UER incursions. Across Africa and South America, the prevailing powers moved to reclaim the last remaining colonies from foreign factions who vowed to defend them.

sections.headline: Global Cataclysm
paragraphs: The world is divided among six great powers. Each of them is riven with ancient grievances, territorial ambitions, threatened borders, humiliating occupations, and entangling alliances.
The stage is set for World War III and a Global Cataclysm…
